title: Reparameterizing Your Object Detectors for Weight Space Programming
read_level: partial (abstract, Secs 1-3.2, experimental setup, main results summary, LLM usage statement, Limitations (App E) and keyword search; proofs, operator details and most appendix tables not read)
why_wsp: Gradient-free closed-form weight edits to object detectors in lifted function-preserving subspaces (moment, 2D-DCT, PCA, Procrustes) then folded back; an LLM (Gemini 4) was used offline as the 'WSP agent' to diagnose and synthesize the reusable operators, with zero LLM calls at edit/runtime.
domain: object detection (MS COCO, COCO-O; YOLO26, EdgeCrafter, RF-DETR)
editor: none (closed-form solver) at edit time; Gemini 4 used offline for "weight-space diagnosis, inverse-reparameterization operator synthesis, experiment orchestration" (LLM Usage Statement)
target: 17 pretrained detectors (YOLO26 N-X, EdgeCrafter S-X, RF-DETR N-L); parameter counts in paper's Table 1 (not extracted)
loop: one-shot (closed-form solve on a calibration set; no LLM loop reported at edit time)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: not reported as fraction; deployed parameter count unchanged: "(∆Params=0%, ∆FLOPs=0%)" (Abstract)

headline_results.claim: Positive COCO gains on all 26 settings at 1.00x cost
headline_results.quote: 1.00× IR-ODWSP achieves 26/26 (100%) positive blind MS COCO gains (up to +0.160 AP and +0.310 APs)

headline_results.claim: Naive binary WSP causes duplicate-box collapse
headline_results.quote: collapsing YOLO26-S/M accuracy by −39.7 to −43.7 AP

headline_results.claim: Zero-image weight repair and label-free weather adaptation
headline_results.quote: repairs corrupted weights with zero images (+2.95 mAP), and gains +2.50– + 2.79 AP under night-and-fog shift
−10% retains 51.62 AP / 33.48 mAP, while positive budgets scale monotonically (+0.30 AP at +10%, +1.12 on RF-DETR-N; 54.83 AP at +100%

cost.claim: No runtime LLM calls; deployment cost unchanged
cost.quote: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs (0 runtime LLM calls). At β = 0% (1.00× cost, ∇ ≡ 0)

baselines_and_controls: Official checkpoints; Vanilla WSP (adapted from Takehi et al.); OD-WSP; collapsed IR-ODWSP (Pure 0%); naive WiSE-FT interpolation; multi-scale+flip TTA; Haar-O(P) controls for the metric proposition
runs_and_variance: single run / not reported (deterministic evaluation across 17 detectors, 26 settings)
robustness_of_edits: zero-shot transfer to COCO-O distribution shifts ("over 85% of 17-model ID gains transfer zero-shot to COCO-O"); adverse-weather adaptation; TensorRT FP16 deployment evaluated
verification: function-preservation of lift/fold operators argued algebraically (Proposition 1, App A) with numerical controls "< 2 × 10−9"; no statistical testing reported
limitations_stated: Absolute AP gain of pure single-checkpoint collapse is bounded (+0.01 to +0.16 AP) since folding cannot raise backbone rank or resolution; larger gains trade latency; cross-model Procrustes alignment requires matching layer widths.
notes_for_survey: Uses the WSP label for gradient-free closed-form detector editing; the LLM's role is offline operator synthesis (disclosed in the LLM usage statement), not per-edit weight writing. Reports that a naive Takehi-style closed-form WSP adaptation degrades 13/17 converged detectors.
